messages:
incident-bot: Paging: high KV cache churn detected in us-west-2 for model 'llama-mqa-v2' (metric: kv_cache_entries_total spike, +420%) — paging oncall-ml. Immediate impact: elevated 95th latency and OOMs on a subset of dedicated pods.

sandeep: saw the alert — I'm on it. which customers are affected?

claire: perf dashboards show 5% of requests now get 502s in dcap-6 pool, 95p latency jumped from 140ms -> 950ms from 02:12 UTC.

oncall-ml: acknowledged. grabbing logs. I'm switching to pager context. @incident-bot can we attach the last deploy for llama-mqa-v2?

incident-bot: Deploy metadata: deploy_id=deploy-2026-03-15-19, rollout: runtime:kv-merge=true enabled at 02:07 UTC; last config change: continuous_batching.max_window_ms changed 250->500 at 02:05 UTC.

dave: that matches my change from earlier — I bumped the batching window to help throughput during peak. Didn't expect kv growth.

eva: quick sanity: is this MQA-specific? any difference vs GQA?

claire: yes looks MQA-only. GQA and non-quantized variants steady. Kernel traces show repeated KV insertions for identical prefix hashes.

sandeep: hypothesis: kv-merge + larger window allows parallel MQA requests to populate duplicate KV entries due to varying prefix alignment (MQA tokenization edge-case). Collisions cause cache blowup and GC pressure.

maria-sre: customer-impact update: two Dedicated tenants (acme-analytics, fintrack) reported degraded throughput + partial errors — support notified.

noncall-ml: triage plan: 1) contain blast radius (disable continuous batching or reduce window) 2) throttle requests to llama-mqa-v2 3) flush KV cache for model instances if safe 4) longer term: revert kv-merge or fix prefix hash dedupe.

dave: I'll revert the batching window change (roll-back 02:25 UTC) and flip kv-merge flag to false for packs in us-west-2.

claire: +1. Also recommend temp pin customers to llama-mqa-v1 (non-MQA) if they need continuity. Need command to flip runtime flag quickly.

sandeep: runbook snippet:

```
# disable continuous batching for model in us-west-2
redwoodctl runtime update --region us-west-2 --model llama-mqa-v2 --set continuous_batching.enabled=false

# or reduce max window
redwoodctl runtime update --region us-west-2 --model llama-mqa-v2 --set continuous_batching.max_window_ms=100

# set kv-merge off
redwoodctl runtime update --region us-west-2 --model llama-mqa-v2 --set runtime.kv_merge=false

# flush kv cache for a model instance
redwoodctl cache flush --region us-west-2 --model-instance i-0abc12345
```

noncall-ml: executing reduce window command now.

incident-bot: Action started: reduce-window by oncall-ml at 02:27:14 UTC.

noncall-ml: result: API returned 200, new window 100ms. I'm seeing immediate drop in kv_churn metric. latency 95p falling from 950ms -> 260ms.

dave: flipping kv-merge=false for the affected runtime in us-west-2 now, will stage then apply.

claire: I'll open a temporary canary that pins traffic away from llama-mqa-v2 to llama-mqa-v1 for the two impacted tenants. Doing policy change for their routes.

maria-sre: informing support: "we've mitigated by reducing batching window and disabling kv-merge in us-west-2; some traffic pinned to non-MQA variant; monitoring for recovery; no data loss expected. ETA to full recovery 30-45m."

sandeep: note: observed pattern — MQA tokenization can produce different token alignment for semantically identical prompts if prefix trimming occurs; kv deduping relied on stable prefix digest that didn't account for MQA subtoken shifts. This interacts especially badly with continuous batching and kv-merge logic that tries to share KV across inflight requests.

eva: do we have a quick mitigant besides revert? maybe a guard that avoids writing duplicate keys when prefix length < config?

dave: for quick patch I can add a heuristic: if token count % 8 != 0 (MQA shard mismatch) skip kv-merge. That's dirty but fast. Will push to staging once we confirm safety.

noncall-ml: kv-merge flag flip completed at 02:34:02 UTC. Post-change metrics: kv_cache_entries_total trending down, pod memory reclaiming, error rate dropping.

incident-bot: Update: incident severity lowered to SEV-2 (partial customer impact mitigated).

claire: customer-facing note drafted for status.redwood: "We observed elevated latencies and partial errors for some Dedicated customers in us-west-2 tied to KV cache growth in llama-mqa-v2. We've reduced batching window and disabled a runtime merge optimization; impacted tenants have been temporarily routed to stable model variants. We're continuing monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem."

maria-sre: posted. Support also provided individual DM updates to Acme + Fintrack. Both reported partial recovery and are monitoring.

sandeep: next steps (post-incident): 1) root cause perf test harness reproducing MQA prefix shifts 2) fix prefix hashing to be alignment-agnostic OR add dedupe layer 3) add telemetry to detect runaway kv growth per-model 4) run a canary of kv-merge=false vs true for varying workloads

dave: I'll own the patch to add MQA-aware prefix normalization + add unit tests. Target: revert quick heuristics within 72h and land proper fix in 2 weeks.

claire: I'll take postmortem owner and timeline for customer communications.

noncall-ml: final status: system stable at 02:40 UTC, 95p latency back to 200-300ms, error rate within normal bounds. Closing the active page but keeping monitoring escalation window open for 2 hours.

incident-bot: Incident closed by oncall-ml at 02:40:08 UTC (note: follow-up tasks created: MQA-prefix-fix, kv-telemetry, canary-plan).

sandeep: thanks team. will update the incident tracker with timeline + metrics + config diffs.

maria-sre: thanks all — support will loop in customers in 24h with postmortem link. :thumbsup:
